subject: Oceanography
title: Antarctic Sea Ice
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Antarctic Sea Ice.

hook.text: Antarctic sea ice doubles the continent's size every winter—then nearly disappears each summer.

buildup.text: Unlike the Arctic, Antarctic ice is mostly seasonal—growing to 18 million km² and shrinking to 3 million.

discovery.text: For decades, Antarctic sea ice was stable or slightly growing—confusing scientists tracking climate change.

twist.text: In 2023, Antarctic sea ice hit record lows—2.5 million km² below the previous record—shocking researchers.

climax.text: The cause remains debated—warming oceans, changed winds, and random variability all play a role.

punchline.text: Antarctica's ice shield held steady for decades—then suddenly didn't.

quiz.question: What happened to Antarctic sea ice in 2023?
options: It hit record lows far below previous records
